chapter: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
title: Kid Ory and not copying anyone
summary: He last played with Ory and Teagarden at Newport; he insists he never copied any trombonist.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: What was your impression of Kid Ory?

Kid Ory? I haven't been around him so many times. The last time we played together was at the, Newport News. We had three trombone players. We had Jack Teagarden, Kid Ory and myself, we played together on the same stand.
The jazz festival, yeah. You know he passed a couple of weeks ago.
Yeah, I know. What was your impression of him as a trombonist?
No, I don't want to make no kind of remark one way or the other. No, I just know he was one of these old-time trombone players, not playing a whole lot of jazz notes, doin' the less slide.
When Kid Ory was playing with Jelly Roll Morton, had you heard him?
not enough... No, that ... I don't remember him. No, I don't.
Because I was wondering what kind of effect the various trombonists had on your style, you know, in the development of ....
I'm not saying it for meanness but so help me God I have never tried to copy from nobody, ( ? ) I don't give a damn, I'm just going to be right or wrong. a colored trombonist, nobody. .... don't want
